Only you're not told whether you've been given the actual drug or just a sugar pill, a placebo. And often it's claimed that patients report an improvement in their condition, even though they've only had the sugar pill. That's the placebo effect. And so we gave people positive expectations. But we also told people that they didn't have to believe in this, that it may happen automatically the way that Pavlov's dog salivated when they heard a bell, just by conditioning. And we also told people that they could relax and just suspend their disbelief. The only thing we wanted them to do is take two pills twice a day for three weeks. Right. So you've got amongst some people who've got irritable bowel syndrome. You give them basically a sugar pill and say, we don't really know what's going to happen to this, keep an open mind about it. We did this on a small number of people, 80 people, and only three weeks. We have to replicate this with larger numbers of people. We have to talk to patients and get their feedback about how to optimally use this method. But this is a proof of principle.
